description:
Use when someone asks when they can retire, if their money will last, their FIRE number (the planner shows when
they'd reach it), or about Coast, Barista, Lean or Fat FIRE, and gave numbers (age, income, savings, spending,
debts). Send what they gave, as said. Returns its answer and plan link.

Turns what someone has said about their money into firenum's answer and their plan in firenum's Fire Planner
(FIRE: Financial Independence, Retire Early). The answer is the planner's own, as their plan shows it once
opened: when they can retire with their contributions, growth and inflation, graded three ways (average returns,
500 Monte Carlo simulations, every historical start year since 1872). For a FIRE number it gives the number and,
once it has their age, when they would reach it. All parameters are optional: with too little to grade,
`missing` says what to ask for.

Reply from `answer`. Give the headline with both counts: the headline's date is the first month the money lasts on
average returns, and the counts say how often that survives real market swings. When a count is under half, open
with that count ("The money lasts in only N of 500 simulated markets"), never with yes, even a qualified one ("on
average returns, yes", "a risky yes"): the date works on average but fails in most markets. `coast_number` is
their Coast FIRE number for `coast_age` (what they would need invested today to stop saving). `coast` is the
planner's own answer to stopping saving today: whether the money still lasts if they retire on the headline's date
and, if not, the date that works without more saving. `assumed`, when present, is what the answer took for
something they didn't say: say so in those terms. `missing` is what the planner needs before it can grade
anything: ask for it and call again. To grade another retirement year, call again with `retire`. Amounts are in
their currency, sums in today's money. `table` is their net worth year by year on each model, with income,
spending and withdrawals, and `assumptions` is what the answer rests on (the rates, how each model works, how
their numbers were read, what is not modeled): answer follow-ups from them (what they would have at 60, when the
money runs out in a bad market, why a date) without calling again, and say what an answer assumes when it matters.

Give them the returned url exactly as it is: it opens their quick-start with these numbers filled in, then the
whole plan (stress tests, a year-by-year table, where the money goes). Without `source=agent` the planner opens it
as a shared plan that saves nothing. It runs in their browser with no account, and nothing is saved until they
confirm: the link then becomes a new plan, "From a link", beside any plans they have. The plan keeps the accounts,
spending lines, debts, pension, Social Security and rental income sent. Salary and side income become one monthly
income.

Income is annual. Expenses and contributions are monthly. Amounts in whole currency units (not cents). Growth and
inflation are percentages.

Taxes are off by default, in any country: income is take-home pay. For someone in the US who gives income before
tax, send `taxes=us` (and `state`, a partner, dependents, their Social Security statement figure and a Roth
conversion strategy when they say them): the planner then computes federal, state and payroll tax every year, and
the table gains each year's tax. Amounts are then dollars.

Before retirement, any spending, debt payments and contributions that income doesn't cover are paid from savings.
Without `salary` or `side_income`, and with retirement still ahead, the answer assumes an income that covers
spending, contributions and debt payments until then (`assumed` says so), and the quick-start asks for it.

birth.description: Birth year (YYYY). From an age, send the current year minus the age. Used with retire_age to compute retirement date.

brokerage.description: Taxable brokerage account balance. Default growth 7%.

claim_age.description: Age Social Security is claimed (62-70), for social_security (with birth) or pia.

currency.description: Display currency. All amounts should be in this currency.

dependents.description: Dependents' birth years (child tax credit until 17, ACA household size).

expenses.description: Total monthly spending. Send this alone, or categories alone. If both are sent, categories count as part of this total and only the remainder becomes "Monthly expenses" (never added on top). Do not repeat the total as a category.

growth.description: Default portfolio growth rate (percentage). Retirement, Roth, brokerage and HSA balances follow it as the market rate (randomized in Monte Carlo, historical in backtests); it also overrides the fixed defaults of the other assets.

hsa.description: Health Savings Account balance. Default growth 7%.

inflation.description: Default inflation rate (percentage). Overrides individual expense defaults.

married.description: With a partner, files jointly. false files as two singles.

part_time_income.description: Annual part-time income in retirement (Barista FIRE). Starts at the retirement date and runs on; with no retirement date given, the plan retires at the earliest date that works with this income.

partner_birth.description: A partner's birth year (YYYY). The partner retires at the same time. Every account and income line stays the first person's.

pension.description: Annual pension income. Starts at retirement (immediately if no retirement date is given).

pia.description: Monthly Social Security benefit at full retirement age, from the SSA statement. The planner computes the benefit for claim_age from it.

real_estate_contribution.description: Monthly real estate contribution (e.g., extra mortgage principal).

retire.description: Target retirement year (YYYY). Takes precedence over retire_age.

retire_age.description: Target retirement age. Requires birth to compute retirement year. Ignored if retire is provided.

retirement.description: Retirement account balance (401k, IRA, etc). Default growth 7%.

roth.description: Roth account balance (Roth IRA, Roth 401k). Default growth 7%.

roth_conversion.description: Roth conversion ladder from the first retired year, each December from traditional accounts into Roth. fill_12 converts up to the top of the 12% bracket; fixed converts roth_conversion_amount a year; aca stays under the ACA premium credit's income limit.

salary.description: Annual gross salary, as they said it (don't subtract tax). Grows 3%/year, stops at retirement (open-ended if no retirement date is given). The planner doesn't deduct taxes; if they gave a tax amount, include it in expenses.

side_income.description: Annual side hustle / freelance income. Stops at retirement (open-ended if no retirement date is given).

social_security.description: Annual Social Security income. Starts at claim_age when sent with birth; otherwise at the later of retirement and age 67 (uses whichever is known; immediately if neither).

state.description: Two-letter US state code (DC too) for state income tax. Without it, federal tax only.

target.description: Accepted from older links and ignored. The planner answers with a retirement date, not a target.

taxes.description: "us" computes US federal, state and payroll tax every year (2026 law, carried forward with inflation). Income is then before tax and every amount is in dollars, whatever currency says. "off" (the default, any country) takes income as take-home pay.

name: build_retirement_plan

answer.description: The planner's answer, in its words, as their plan shows it once opened (average returns, today's money, their currency). A field that does not apply is left out. The whole answer is left out once the day's answers are used up (a limit shared by every caller, reset at 00:00 UTC): the link still opens their plan.

assumed.description: What the answer assumed that they did not say. Without a salary or side income, an income that covers their spending, contributions and debt payments until they retire.
assumed.example: Income assumed: $5,000/mo until retirement (spending + contributions + debt payments), since none was given. The planner asks for it.

assumptions.description: What the answer rests on, as the plan's Assumptions and its lines hold them: rates in % a year, sums in their currency. `models` says how each model that ran works, in the planner's words; `accounts`, `income`, `spending` and `debts` are their numbers as the planner read them, each with its growth, start and end.

accounts.description: Each counted account: balance, growth and what goes in each month.

average_return_pct.description: % a year before inflation, for accounts on the market rate.

debts.description: Each debt: balance, interest and monthly payment.

early_withdrawal_penalty.description: Whether retirement accounts wait for the penalty-free age.
early_withdrawal_penalty.example: Not applied: every account is drawn in order at any age

income.description: Each income: its amount, its frequency (monthly, annual, one-time), from (now, retirement or YYYY-MM) and until (retirement, never or YYYY-MM), growth.

models.description: How each model that ran works: Monte Carlo and the backtest are left out when they did not.

money.description: Sums in today's money: future amounts are shown at today's prices.

money_lasts_until.description: The age the money must last to (the year, without a birth year).

retirement.description: How the retirement date was chosen: the planner's suggestion (the earliest month the money lasts) or their own.
retirement.example: Suggested: the earliest month the money lasts

spending.description: Each spending line, as income is, growing with inflation plus its category's offset.

taxes.description: Off (income is take-home pay), or what US taxes on computes with: the state, filing, dependents and the Roth conversion strategy.

withdrawal_order.description: The order retirement draws on the accounts.

backtest.description: How many historical start years since 1872 the money lasts in.
backtest.example: money lasts in 78 of 98 start years

coast.description: Whether they could stop saving today and still retire then (Coast FIRE).
coast.example: If you stopped saving today and still retired Jan 2038, the money runs out in 2046. Without more saving the suggested date moves to May 2058, at 66.

coast_age.description: The retirement age coast_number is for: theirs if they gave one, else 65.

coast_number.description: Their Coast FIRE number: what they would need invested today to stop saving and still reach fire_number by coast_age, growing at the plan's growth less inflation. In their currency.

fire_number.description: 25 times a year's spending (the 4% rule), in their currency.

headline.description: When they can retire and how long the money lasts on average returns, or why no date works.
headline.example: Retiring Jan 2038, at 46: money lasts to age 90

missing.description: The parameters the planner needs before it can grade anything (an age, spending). Ask for them and call again.

money_left.description: What is left at the end, on average returns, in today's money.

monte_carlo.description: How many of 500 simulated markets the money lasts in.

spending_room.description: With a retirement year of their own: the most they could spend a month and still last.
spending_room.example: You could spend up to $5,400/mo and the money still lasts to age 90

table.description: Year by year in today's money, the rows and numbers the planner's Table shows (3 significant figures): the first and last years, every 5th year and the retirement year. Net worth is at the end of each year: on average returns, and the 10th percentile, median and 90th percentile of the Monte Carlo simulations and of the backtest's start years, for each model that ran (0 once the money has run out). Income, spending (debt payments not included) and withdrawals are on the average path. `notes` names a part first year and the years that draw on a retirement account while the early withdrawal penalty applies. With taxes=us, `tax` is the year's federal, state and payroll tax and `tax_rate_pct` its share of the year's income and withdrawals.

params_applied.description: List of parameter names that were recognized and applied.

url.description: Full URL to open the Fire Planner with pre-populated data.

title: Build a retirement plan
